text:
support_jane: Customer reports sudden 400s from /v1/embeddings after a deploy. Used to work earlier today, now failing for a batch job.
marc_engineer: Do we have the request/err body?
support_jane: Pasted what customer sent (redacted):
```curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","input":{"text":"hello world"}}'
```
marc_engineer: Yep, there's the issue — they're passing input as an object (with a nested \"text\" key). The embeddings API expects input to be a string or an array of strings. That payload triggers a 400: \"input must be string or array of strings; got object\". :eyes:
raj_ops: Also watch for array-of-objects vs array-of-strings. Lots of clients accidentally send [{"text":"a"},{"text":"b"}] instead of ["a","b"]. Our server will reject both schemas.
sally_dev: Another common trap — NDJSON/gzip vs application/json. If they gzip NDJSON but keep Content-Type: application/json we sometimes parse incorrectly and return 400/415.
support_jane: Customer error text: \"400 Bad Request - embeddings: input must be string or array of strings; received object\"
marc_engineer: Repro locally — failing curl above returns the same 400. Changing to either of these will work: one-off
```curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","input":"hello world"}'
```
or batch:
```curl
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer REDACTED\" \
  -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","input":["one","two","three"]}'
```
marc_engineer: Also note model dims — customer later said they expect 1024 dims but model returns 1536. That's a downstream index mismatch, not an API error. Clarify which model their index expects.
support_jane: They said they migrated to redwood-embed-large yesterday but forgot to reindex the downstream store.
raj_ops: For high-throughput ingest, they tried batches of ~2048 and saw timeouts/rate-limit errors. Recommend limiting batch sizes to <=512 for stability and using our bulk ingest job or streaming mechanism. Batching too large also amplifies schema mistakes.
sally_dev: I'll add a short snippet to the docs noting common JS mistakes (fetch/axios double-encoding, passing objects instead of strings, mixing JSONL with application/json).
support_jane: I sent corrected payload examples and repro steps to the customer. Asked them to confirm model and reindex target.
embed-bot: :robot_face: Created incident note INC-2026-142 (embed-schema-mismatch) and assigned to marc_engineer.
marc_engineer: Drafting a templated reply including: 1) Why object vs array errors happen, 2) Example payloads that work, 3) Batch size guidance, 4) How to check model dims (we show expected vector length in model catalog), 5) Quick reindex checklist.
support_jane: Customer tried the corrected single/batch payload and got embeddings back (1536 dims) and no 400s. They'll reindex and confirm ingest success.
marc_engineer: Closing on our side once customer confirms downstream match. Leaving a note to consider a tighter error message that includes \"expected string or array\" vs generic schema error.
support_jane: Thanks team.
